scope: Theorem 5.4 (Outer representation interface) of the manuscript “The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction” (preprints/The-PCP-for-PPAD-conjecture-a-quasilinear-reduction-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 136 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a7ab4d86183890be), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 47-48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: There are fixed positive constants δraw, ρraw, fixed integers CL, craw, and uniform deterministic algorithms with the following properties for every End-of-Line input of length N. They construct a directed graph of valid extended labels, represented by canonical words Rv ∈ ({0, 1}L )Γ , |Γ| = N poly(ℓN ), L = (ℓN + Cbase)CL , ℓN = ⌈log2(N + 2)⌉, where Cbase may be any sufficiently large fixed integer. (i) Graph and endpoint data. The graph has indegree and outdegree at most one, no self-edges, and no isolated vertices. It has the public distinguished source v∗ and actual successor v+ ∗ in (5.7); their entire words are computable in poly(N) time. Every other endpoint is mapped in poly(N) time to a nonzero solution of the input End-of-Line instance. Every canonical word is computable from its valid label in polynomial time. (ii) Distance and valid-word testing. Distinct canonical words have normalized symbol distance at least δraw. A uniform center test has perfect completeness and uses only a fixed finite list Π of permutation-neighbors, of cardinality q independent of N. For every fixed α > 0 there is a fixed θα > 0 such that rej(W) < θα =⇒ dist(W, Rv) < α for some valid v. 47 Also rej(W) ≤ q dist(W, Rv) for every valid v. (iii) Local proposals and flags. At each requested center, total deterministic routines on Π(k) compute a next or previous proposed symbol and an existence bit. On Rv the bit is independent of the center and equals the actual edge-existence flag. If it is one, the proposed symbols form exactly the canonical neighboring word; if it is zero, the default proposal is Rv itself. (iv) Value-independent uncertainty correction. There is a total local one-round corrector with a bounded permutation neighborhood. If |U|/|Γ| ≤ ρraw, it maps every word agreeing with Rv outside U to a word agreeing with Rv outside a set U+ determined only by U, with |U+| ≤ |U|/2. Consequently t rounds leave a prescribed uncertainty support of density at most 2−t|U|/|Γ|. The guarantee holds for arbitrary values on U. Different requested-center simulations may use different values there, provided repeated occurrences of a position are consistent within each individual cone. (v) Global recovery. From any word within ρraw symbol distance of a valid word, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm recovers its exact extended label and raw word. It then recovers the logical bits by systematic coefficient extraction and evaluation on the subgroup. In particular it extracts an End-of-Line answer whenever the recovered label is a nonexceptional endpoint. (vi) Uniform cost and order of choices. The total raw data and listed public descriptions have N poly(ℓN ) bits and are constructible in poly(N) time. Each raw local test, proposed symbol, flag, and one-round corrector has a Boolean circuit of size at most CLcraw on a fixed number of symbols. For each fixed t, correction for t rounds followed by any such raw routine has size at most CtLcraw and at most O(Qt) symbol ports, with uniform construction for that t. The exponents CL, craw are fixed before t and any later port arity. Further fixed additive padding in Cbase has only linear processing cost and does not change these exponents or arities.
